correctness.rationale: For the symmetric payoff matrix the payoff difference is c(1/2-x). Dividing the positive interior factor x(1-x)[x^k+(1-x)^k] out of the ODE leaves lambda z/2-H_k(z) with z=1-2x and H_k(z)=tanh(k artanh z). For 0<k<1 and 0<z<1, H_k(z)<z and H_k'(z)=k(1-H_k(z)^2)/(1-z^2). Its second derivative has sign z-kH_k(z)>0, so the quotient H_k(z)/z strictly increases from k to 1. For k>=1 the quotient is at least 1 and lambda/2<1. This yields the entire equilibrium census, and the strict sign changes give the basins by uniqueness and monotone bounded convergence on the invariant interval. At the admissible equality lambda=2k, expansion of H_k near zero gives the positive cubic drift 2^(2-k) k(1-k^2)(x-1/2)^3/3 with fifth-order remainder; the center repels even though its linear derivative vanishes. Endpoints have slope -(1-lambda/2) and remain attracting. In the example, dividing the bracket by sqrt(1-x) and clearing 9(1+t^2), t=sqrt(x/(1-x)), gives exactly 2(t-2)(t-1)(2t-1); its three positive roots yield the stated witness. Differentiating this factored bracket gives slopes 2 sqrt(5)/75 at 1/5 and 4/5 and -sqrt(2)/36 at 1/2; all five equilibria are hyperbolic in the witness.
residual_risks: The equality case only concerns 0<k<1 under lambda<2. The ODE classification does not assert finite-population chain behavior or a global asymmetric-payoff classification.

value.rationale: The payoff ratio makes the ordinary mixed equilibrium exactly central, so the line isolates the effect of complexity on coexistence without moving that equilibrium. Determining the exact parameter slice supporting survival of a stable mixed state alongside both pure attractors, rather than merely locating a local derivative crossing, sharpens the existing broad phase table and specifies the initial-condition thresholds. The hyperbolic witness also shows the pattern is not an artifact requiring exact symmetry.
residual_risks: Value is for the stated continuum game and motivated symmetry slice; it does not give a full payoff-space diagram or stochastic prediction.
